page.overview:
What is House of Elros?

The House of Elros was the line of Elros' descendants. Due to his ancestry, he was Half-elven, and given the choice of the immortality of the Eldar, or the Gift of Ilúvatar. He chose to live as a mortal, but he had an extraordinary lifespan of 500 years. His descendants inherited his longevity, but Elros was the only one who lived so long, as well as the longest-lived mortal human.

Elros, also known as Tar-Minyatur, was the first King of Númenor. After his time, the island was ruled by Kings and Queens of his house for about 3,278 years of the Second Age. Elros' distant descendant Ar-Pharazôn was manipulated by Sauron into bringing about the Downfall of Númenor, and ended the Line of the Kings of Númenor.

The House of Elros, however, survived the Downfall and continued in exile. The kings descended through Tar-Meneldur, but another branch of the House also survived: the Lords of Andúnië, descended from Meneldur's elder sister Silmariën. The line of the Lords of Andúnië continued through Elendil and his sons, Isildur and Anarion. This bloodline of Elros came to Middle-earth, surviving through the Kings of Arnor and of Gondor. After the War of the Ring, and many millennia after its founder's death, one known heir of the House of Elros was still alive, Aragorn II, who eventually established the Reunited Kingdom of Arnor and Gondor.
